synopsis: 47 tests across 14 suites executed; one historical test produced four failed expectations. New independent competency preservation conflicts with that older test whose name and assertions require a newly started incomplete equivalent check to erase all completed history.

failures.diagnosis: The historical test expects practice 0 with assessed count 0 immediately after starting a later check, then practice 0 with assessed count 1 after only continuity is answered. Those expectations encode the erasure the new requirement forbids.
failures.fix: Rename and rewrite the historical test around per-competency preservation: after later empty check, retain all four completed competencies; after later failed continuity, supersede continuity only while retaining the other three. Under the current four-equal-competency fixture the intended expectations are initially 100/4 and then 75/4. Keep eligible prior answers intact and check the new answer only replaces its exact scope.

recommendations: Do not revert the new preservation behavior to satisfy the historical erasure assertions. Reconcile both test suites to the explicit user requirement.
Rerun the entire same selected set after the expectation update. New preservation, opening reclassification, matrix and integrated AI suites did not produce additional failures in this run.
limitations: Raw failure output does not include actual numeric values for the failed expressions; recommended values derive from authored fixture/rubric semantics and need a fresh passing run.
No live provider or native scoring presentation claim follows from this portable test.
